record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let P_α(z) = exp(2πiα)z + z², where α is an irrational Bruno number, and let S_α be the maximal connected open neighborhood of 0 on which P_α is analytically linearizable. Does there exist such an α for which the boundary ∂S_α is a C¹ submanifold of the complex plane, equivalently a circle?

evidence.quote: Does there exist α1 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα1 (the boundary of Sα1) is a C1 submanifold of C (a circle) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an irrational number $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ with continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$, say that $\alpha$ is a Bruno number if
$$\sum_{n\ge 0}\frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}<\infty.$$
Consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}\,z+z^2,\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}.$$
By a theorem of Bruno–Siegel, if $\alpha$ is a Bruno number then $P_\alpha$ is analytically linearizable in a neighborhood of $0$, i.e. there is a holomorphic injection $\varphi$ defined on an open disk around $0$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi'(0)=1$, conjugating $P_\alpha$ to the rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$. Let $S_\alpha$ denote the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$, defined as the maximal connected open neighborhood of $0$ on which $P_\alpha$ is analytically linearizable.

Question: Does there exist a Bruno number $\alpha$ such that the boundary $\partial S_\alpha$ is a $C^1$ submanifold of $\mathbb{C}$ (equivalently, a topological circle that is $C^1$-smooth)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively (in a much stronger form) by Avila, Buff, and Chéritat, who proved the existence of a dense uncountable set of Bruno-type rotation numbers $\alpha$ for which the quadratic polynomial $P_\alpha$ has a Siegel disk with $C^\infty$-smooth boundary (a Jordan curve which is in particular a $C^1$ submanifold of $\mathbb{C}$). The result appeared in "Siegel disks with smooth boundaries," Acta Mathematica 193 (2004), 1–30.

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks with smooth boundaries (Avila–Buff–Chéritat), Acta Math.
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a dense uncountable set of angles α such that the quadratic polynomial P_α has a Siegel disk with C^∞-smooth boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of quadratic Siegel disks with C^∞ (hence C^1) boundaries was established, providing a positive answer.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Siegel disks with smooth boundaries — Buff & Chéritat (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of α (Bruno numbers) for which the boundary of the Siegel disk of P_α is a smooth Jordan curve.
status_evidence.claim: Bruno numbers α exist with ∂S_α a smooth (hence C^1) submanifold of C.
